title: PIN-01: PinResolver.resolve() leaks allocator-owned PinnedVersion fields on every error path after Step 3/AC3/AC4
summary: src/engine/pin_resolver.zig's PinResolver.resolve() allocates each PinnedVersion's resolved_id/version (and, for the variable_schema entry, ref) via the caller's long-lived allocator parameter, not the function's local arena. The ONLY cleanup for these allocator-owned strings is in the SUCCESS path (the loop building the final 'owned' slice, which explicitly frees them after duplicating). Every error return before that point -- validateVariableSchema()'s VariableSchemaViolation, applyPinOverrides()'s UnresolvedPinOverride, and any PoolExhausted/TransactionFailed from either -- returns immediately via 'try', leaking every allocator-owned field already stored in pins.items at that point. Confirmed live via Zig's DebugAllocator: tests/integration/pin01_ac345_resolution_test.zig's TC-PIN-01-04 (an UnresolvedPinOverride case) reports 13 leaked allocations.

root_cause.details: resolve()'s arena (arena.deinit() via defer) only frees the arena's OWN allocations (the ArrayList backing storage, extractStringField's service_id copies) -- it has no effect on allocator-owned memory. No errdefer or equivalent covers the same cleanup the success-path loop performs, on any of the function's several early-return error paths after at least one PinnedVersion has been appended.

resolution: Added errdefer immediately after pins starts being populated in PinResolver.resolve() that walks pins.items and frees each entry's allocator-owned resolved_id, version, and (for variable_schema entries) ref fields, mirroring the cleanup the success-path loop already performs. Covers all error return paths: VariableSchemaViolation (validateVariableSchema), UnresolvedPinOverride (applyPinOverrides), PoolExhausted, and TransactionFailed.
verification: TC-PIN-01-04 (UnresolvedPinOverride error path) no longer reports leaked allocations under Zig DebugAllocator.
prevention: Add an errdefer immediately after pins starts being populated that walks pins.items and frees each entry's allocator-owned fields the same way the success path's cleanup loop already does, mirroring the errdefer pattern already used later in the same function around the 'owned' allocation.

When a function separates an arena allocator (for transient/local state) from a caller-supplied allocator (for returned/long-lived state) inside the same loop, audit every early-return path for whether caller-allocator-owned state accumulated so far needs explicit cleanup -- the arena's own defer does not cover it.
